To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) The best achievable rate for lossy compression of an arbitrary source with respect to an arbitrary distortion measure is the rate of the minimum entropy distribution.

(a) for any arbitrary source, there exists a codebook with redundancy bounded by (d/2)(log n + log log n + O(1)), where n is the number of source samples and d is the dimensionality of the source; (b) for a stationary ergodic source, the redundancy of the codebook can be made arbitrarily close to (d/2 log n) with probability one.

the performance of lossy data compression algorithms is characterized by the following: The best achievable rate for a fixed distortion is equal to the minimum of the rate-distortion function and the rate-distortion redundancy function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of general coding theorems for arbitrary source models.
the fundamental limits on lossy compression, and the design of practical compression algorithms that approach the theoretical limits.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we are able to characterize the performance of arbitrary compression algorithms for arbitrary sources, and with arbitrary distortion measures.
the redundancy in the optimal Bayesian codebook is of order (d/2)(log n) bits.

the redundancy of a universal Bayesian codebook is bounded above by a constant times log n, where n is the number of codewords in the codebook, and d is the dimension (or number of parameters) of the simplex.
we have developed a theory of lossy data compression which, while not as simple as Shannon's theory of lossless compression, is still quite simple and powerful.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of rate-distortion theory, the notion of a codebook is more general than the notion of a probability measure on a fixed alphabet.
the performance of compression algorithms can be characterized by the performance of a probability measure on the reproduction alphabet.
the performance of compression algorithms can be analyzed in terms of the probability measures on the reconstruction alphabet induced by the code.
